name: Sika Rugasol FC
paste:
SIKA® RUGASOL® FC: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Rugasol® FC, February 2026, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sika-rugasol-fc.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Rugasol® FC where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2026, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description. Sika® Rugasol® FC is a gel retarder specially designed for the production of exposed aggregate finishes or for producing a mechanical key to construction joints, stop ends for subsequent rendering applications on vertical surfaces.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC surface retarder is used to expose aggregate on formed Portland Cement based concrete surfaces.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC provides an efficient, economical method of obtaining a rough bonding surface without the need for hacking, chipping, or sandblasting.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC is also used to produce precast panels having a decorative architectural finish showing the colour and texture of natural aggregate. The aggregate remains whole and unbroken.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC is painted directly on formwork for walls, ceilings, vertical construction joints or any similar formed concrete surface.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC dries on the formwork to a tough, but water-soluble film. Protect from rain. Forms may be coated before or after erection. Reinforcing steel is placed as usual.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC will retard the set of the cement paste by up to 6 mm (¼”) depth, the depth depends upon the thickness of the coating, the time elapsed before the retarder is removed, the cement content of the concrete and the quantity of water in the mix. The ambient temperature will also affect the depth of retardation.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Rugasol® FC
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Liquid retarder for vertical concrete surfaces
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (February 2026, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC will only delay the ultimate hardening and do not “kill” the set of the cement.
    - When used correctly, Sika® Rugasol® FC will not stain concrete, even white concrete.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC will not affect the bond of reinforcement to concrete if accidental splashing occurs, provided it is thoroughly cleaned with clean water.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC is solvent free.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Whitish gel
    - Density: Approximately 1.05 kg/l at 23º C
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 205 liter drum; 10 liter pail
    - Shelf life: Protected from direct sunlight and frost, the shelf life is 12 months.
    - Storage conditions: Store Sika® Rugasol® FC at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C, protected from direct sunlight and frost.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (February 2026, Version 01.02) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (February 2026, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Consumption: Approximately 0.3 l/m²
4.3 Application.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC is ready for use from the container. It should be stirred before use and must not be diluted.
    - Sika® Rugasol® FC may be applied to any type of clean form. Apply to heavy coat with a brush or roller, and allow to dry (normally 2 to 4 hours in mild temperatures). No mould oils should be on the forms. Coated surfaces should be protected from strong sunlight. Sika® Rugasol® FC dries on the formwork to create a tough, but water-soluble film that must be protected from rain.
    - Exposed aggregate: For optimum results forms should be removed as soon as possible after the concrete is poured, normally not later than one day in warm weather and up to 2 days in cold weather. If the forms must remain in place longer use two or even three coats of Sika® Rugasol® FC to ensure deep penetration. A mock-up of the construction element should be tested first to see if the outcome meets the requirements.
    - Cleaning off: Some of the soft cement paste will stick to the form when the shuttering is stripped; this can be removed easily while still soft from both the formwork and concrete by a light wire-brushing or with a high pressure water jet.
    - Always clean off immediately after stripping the shutters as the soft cement paste soon hardens, the concrete should be kept moist and cured as usual. It is advisable to undertake a small test in all cases prior to use, as cements and conditions of use can change from site to site.
    - When using untreated wood or porous forms for the first time we recommend a minimum of two coats of Sika® Rugasol® FC. This will impregnate the surface and aid in the uniform exposure of the aggregate. Form panels to be re-used may be scraped off and recoated with Sika® Rugasol® FC as soon as it is required.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations. Sika® Rugasol® FC only retards the surface setting of the concrete and does not stop the set. If the surface is not washed off within the retarding period, the concrete will set and reach ultimate strength. Thereafter the surface will be difficult to remove.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (February 2026, Version 01.02) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Exposed aggregate: For optimum results forms should be removed as soon as possible after the concrete is poured, normally not later than one day in warm weather and up to 2 days in cold weather. If the forms must remain in place longer use two or even three coats of Sika® Rugasol® FC to ensure deep penetration. A mock-up of the construction element should be tested first to see if the outcome meets the requirements.
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Rugasol® FC, February 2026, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/c/sika-rugasol-fc.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika® Rugasol® FC, version 02/04/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sds-sika-rugasolfc.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
